name: 14-Phenylpropoxymetopon
summary: 14-Phenylpropoxymetopon (PPOM) is an opioid analogue that is a derivative of metopon which has been substituted with a γ-phenylpropoxy group at the 14-position. PPOM is a highly potent analgesic drug several thousand times stronger than morphine, with an even higher in vivo potency than etorphine.

pharmacology.text: The 14-phenylpropoxy substitution appears to confer potent μ-opioid agonist activity, even when combined with substitutions such as N-cyclopropyl or N-allyl, which normally result in μ-opioid antagonist compounds.

uses.text: It has never been used in humans, but would be expected to produce effects similar to those of other potent opioid agonists, including strong analgesia, sedation, euphoria, constipation, itching and respiratory depression which could be harmful or fatal.

sideEffects.en: It has never been used in humans. It would be expected to cause strong sedation, euphoria, itching, constipation and slowed breathing, and at its extreme strength an overdose could easily be fatal.
sideEffects.zh: 它從未在人體使用過。預期會造成強烈鎮靜、欣快、搔癢、便祕與呼吸變慢，以它極高的效力，過量很容易致命。
sideEffects.zhHans: 它从未在人体使用过。预期会造成强烈镇静、欣快、搔痒、便秘与呼吸变慢，以它极高的效力，过量很容易致命。

fact.en: Its phenylpropoxy group is so powerful that even versions carrying N-allyl or N-cyclopropyl groups, changes that normally turn an opioid into a blocker like naloxone, stay strong agonists.
fact.zh: 它的苯丙氧基作用極強，即使帶上N-烯丙基或N-環丙基（這些改變通常會把鴉片類藥物變成像納洛酮那樣的阻斷劑），仍然是強效促效劑。
fact.zhHans: 它的苯丙氧基作用极强，即使带上N-烯丙基或N-环丙基（这些改变通常会把鸦片类药物变成像纳洛酮那样的阻断剂），仍然是强效促效剂。
